hypotheses.reasoning: The /v1/notify 502s are the gateway's symptom: api-gateway reports 'upstream notification-svc connection reset (no healthy upstream)'. The origin is notification-svc memory exhaustion. Old-gen heap stopped being reclaimed by about 20:49:18 (#1719: 78% after full GC, old gen not reclaimed), worsened by 20:52:45 (#2171: 87%, GC overhead 35%). It then hit OutOfMemoryError in messageCache.put (#2250) and the pod was OOMKilled at its 2Gi limit (#2253). Repeated OOM kills followed (#2479, #2482, #2645, #2647). Each restart drops the pod, so gateway calls fail in bursts until it comes back. The cache keeps growing with no eviction, which points to an unbounded messageCache (leak-like growth). Other services have no errors on the notify path. The catalog-svc 401s on translation (#2300, #2383) and the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts are separate issues that affect search and status, not notify. The earlier template-svc slow render (#1118) is a minor warning and not the cause.

Slow template-svc render (2975ms, #1118) could cause notification-svc to hold more in-flight messages and grow memory. It is only a single soft-threshold warning and template-svc reports no errors, so this is weak evidence.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restart is only a temporary fix. Capture a heap dump from notification-svc to identify what is retaining messageCache entries. Add a size bound or TTL/eviction to messageCache and roll back to the last known-good build if the growth started with a recent change. Raise the memory limit only as a stopgap. Separately, rotate the catalog-svc translation API key (401 invalid_api_key, #2300/#2383), which breaks search, and investigate the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts in status-poller.

hypotheses.reasoning: The /v1/notify 502s are the gateway's symptom: api-gateway reports 'upstream notification-svc connection reset (no healthy upstream)'. The origin is notification-svc memory exhaustion. Old-gen heap stopped being reclaimed by about 20:49:18 (#1719: 78% after full GC, old gen not reclaimed), worsened by 20:52:45 (#2171: 87%, GC overhead 35%). It then hit OutOfMemoryError in messageCache.put (#2250) and the pod was OOMKilled at its 2Gi limit (#2253). Repeated OOM kills followed (#2479, #2482, #2645, #2647). Each restart drops the pod, so gateway calls fail in bursts until it comes back. The cache keeps growing with no eviction, which points to an unbounded messageCache (leak-like growth). Other services have no errors on the notify path. The catalog-svc 401s on translation (#2300, #2383) and the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts are separate issues that affect search and status, not notify. The earlier template-svc slow render (#1118) is a minor warning and not the cause.

Slow template-svc render (2975ms, #1118) could cause notification-svc to hold more in-flight messages and grow memory. It is only a single soft-threshold warning and template-svc reports no errors, so this is weak evidence.

input.recommendedAction: Restart is only a temporary fix. Capture a heap dump from notification-svc to identify what is retaining messageCache entries. Add a size bound or TTL/eviction to messageCache and roll back to the last known-good build if the growth started with a recent change. Raise the memory limit only as a stopgap. Separately, rotate the catalog-svc translation API key (401 invalid_api_key, #2300/#2383), which breaks search, and investigate the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts in status-poller.
